title: Things to Do in Aizawl: Ridge Views, Mizo Culture & Day Trips to Reiek
seoTitle: Things to Do in Aizawl: Views, Culture & Day Trips | Kudozz Club
description: Things to do in Aizawl: Solomon's Temple, Durtlang Hills, the Mizoram State Museum, Bara Bazar, KV Paradise, Reiek's heritage village, Tamdil Lake, Hmuifang, Vantawng Falls and Chapchar Kut with its bamboo dance.
dek: Mizoram's capital, stacked along a steep ridge above the Tlawng valley, known for its quiet streets, church choirs and bamboo-dance festivals.
searchIntent: Travellers planning two to four days in Aizawl and nearby Mizoram, looking for sights and cultural experiences.

hero.alt: Aizawl city buildings on the ridge
hero.caption: Aizawl

intro: Aizawl, at about 1,130 metres, is the capital of Mizoram, built along steep ridges with buildings stepping down the hillsides. The Mizo people are mostly Christian, and churches, choirs and community life are central to the city. Aizawl is also known for its orderly traffic, where drivers queue patiently and rarely use their horns.

Things to do in Aizawl include viewpoints such as Durtlang Hills, Solomon's Temple, the State Museum and Bara Bazar, and day trips to Reiek's heritage village, Tamdil Lake, Hmuifang and Vantawng Falls. March brings Chapchar Kut, the spring festival with the famous bamboo dance, cheraw.
Two days covers the city; add one or two for day trips. Indian nationals need an Inner Line Permit, available online or on arrival at the airport.

items.name: Visit Solomon's Temple
body: Solomon's Temple, a large white church built by the Kohhran Thianghlim denomination, is one of Aizawl's landmarks, with landscaped grounds and views over the city. Visitors are welcome outside service times.

items.name: Watch sunrise from Durtlang Hills
body: Durtlang Hills, on the northern edge of Aizawl, gives panoramic views of the city and the surrounding ridges. Sunrise, with mist in the valleys, is especially beautiful.

items.name: See the Mizoram State Museum
body: The State Museum has displays of Mizo costumes, textiles, weapons, musical instruments and historical artefacts, and explains the traditions of Mizo communities.

items.name: Walk through Bara Bazar
body: Bara Bazar is the main market, with stalls selling vegetables, meat, Mizo textiles such as the puan (wrap skirt), and imported goods from Myanmar. It is lively in the morning.

items.name: See KV Paradise
body: KV Paradise, in Durtlang, is a three-storey marble mausoleum built by a man in memory of his wife, sometimes called Mizoram's Taj Mahal. It has a garden and views.

items.name: See the Bara Bazar lanes and Millennium Centre
body: Around Bara Bazar, the Millennium Centre and the lanes of shops sell everything from electronics to traditional puan textiles and bamboo goods. Look for Mizo shawls and the colourful puanchei worn at weddings and festivals.

items.name: Visit Reiek

image.alt: Traditional Mizo houses at Reiek Heritage Village
image.caption: Reiek Heritage Village

body: Reiek, about 30 km from Aizawl, has a heritage village with traditional Mizo houses, including a bachelors' dormitory (zawlbuk) and houses of a chief and a widow. A walk up Reiek Tlang gives views as far as Bangladesh on clear days.

items.name: Picnic at Tamdil Lake
body: Tamdil, a natural lake surrounded by forest about 85 km from Aizawl, has boating and a tourist resort. A local legend explains its origin from a giant mustard plant.

items.name: Walk on Hmuifang
body: Hmuifang, a forested hill about 50 km south of Aizawl, has been protected since the time of Mizo chiefs and is a good place for walks and birdwatching.

items.name: See Vantawng Falls
body: Vantawng Falls, near Thenzawl in Serchhip district, drops in two tiers through thick forest and is one of the highest waterfalls in Mizoram. It is seen from a viewpoint across the gorge. Thenzawl is also known for handloom weaving.

items.name: Visit Champhai
body: Champhai, near the Myanmar border in the east, has wide rice fields, vineyards and viewpoints over the hills, and is known for its grapes and wine. It is a long drive from Aizawl and best with a night's stay.

items.name: Watch cheraw at Chapchar Kut
body: Chapchar Kut, held in March after the jungle is cleared for jhum cultivation, is Mizoram's biggest festival. Its highlight is cheraw, the bamboo dance, in which dancers step nimbly between clapping bamboo poles.

items.name: Hear a church choir
body: Mizo choirs are known for their harmonies. Sunday services and choral competitions are a moving experience; visitors are welcome if they are respectful.

items.name: Eat Mizo food
body: Try bai (a vegetable stew with bamboo shoot), vawksa rep (smoked pork), sawhchiar (rice porridge with meat) and fresh chutneys. Food is usually mild, with chilli served on the side.

items.name: Winter (November to February)
body: Cool, clear days and good views from the ridges. Christmas is celebrated across the city with lights, carols and community feasts, and it is one of the most festive times to visit.

items.name: Spring (March to April)
body: Chapchar Kut brings dances and music in March. The weather warms up but stays pleasant.

items.name: Monsoon (May to September)
body: Heavy rain and occasional landslides on the roads into Mizoram. The hills are green, but travel can be disrupted.

byTraveller.text: Time a visit for Chapchar Kut and spend Sunday listening to a choir.
Stay a few days, walk the ridges and enjoy the city's unhurried pace.

oneDay: Watch sunrise from Durtlang Hills and visit KV Paradise. After breakfast, see the State Museum and walk through Bara Bazar. Visit Solomon's Temple in the afternoon and end at a viewpoint over the city at sunset.
tips: Lengpui Airport is about 30 km from Aizawl; a new rail link to Sairang near Aizawl has also opened.
Apply for the Mizoram ILP online or get it on arrival at Lengpui Airport.
Sundays are very quiet, with most businesses closed.
Follow local traffic etiquette: no honking and no queue-jumping.

faqs.q: What are the best things to do in Aizawl?
faqs.a: Visit Solomon's Temple, Durtlang Hills, the State Museum, Bara Bazar and KV Paradise, and take day trips to Reiek, Tamdil Lake, Hmuifang and Vantawng Falls.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for Aizawl?
faqs.a: Yes. Indian nationals need an Inner Line Permit for Mizoram.

faqs.q: How many days are enough for Aizawl?
faqs.a: Two days for the city; three to four with day trips.
